articles.title: Jasprit Bumrah, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi on Afghanistan's radar: Ibrahim Zadran reveals plans
articles.summary: Cricket News: Afghanistan captain Ibrahim Zadran says his team has made specific plans to deal with Jasprit Bumrah in Sunday's opening T20I against India at the Aru.
articles.body: Afghanistan captain Ibrahim Zadran says his team has made specific plans to deal with Jasprit Bumrah in Sunday's opening T20I against India at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in New Delhi.Bumrah is set to return to international cricket after missing matches due to a left knee injury. His return gives India another major option with the ball, but Zadran said Afghanistan will not make things complicated while facing the star pacer."If you look at Jasprit Bumrah, he is one of the best, and he is my favourite fast bowler. We as a group never think things in a complicated way for ourselves. So we have a very good plan for him, and we just thought about him, how to play against him, and hopefully we are going to play better cricket against Jasprit Bumrah or the Indian Cricket Team," Zadran told reporters in a press conference on Saturday.Sooryavanshi also on Afghanistan's radarAfghanistan have also prepared for India's teenage batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi.The Afghanistan team has used information from players who have faced the left-handed opener in the IPL. Zadran said they have also studied videos of Sooryavanshi before the series."He is an amazing talent. Recently, he played great cricket in the Indian Premier League (IPL), and he has been performing well at a different level in cricket events. We have thought about him, and we have gained that knowledge from those guys who have played against him in the IPL.“We have already watched his videos, and we just try to keep it very simple for ourselves, just to execute the right plans at the right time against him. We are just trying to make things simple for us, not complicated," he stated.Zadran takes over T20I captaincyZadran has taken over the T20I captaincy from Rashid Khan. He believes their strong relationship will help Afghanistan make a fresh start after their early exit from the T20 World Cup.The new captain also feels Afghanistan's experience of playing in India will be useful."I would say, I was destined to have a captain like Rashid Khan. Alongside him, we had better communication, better understanding between us. When he was a captain, I was helping him as a vice-captain, and the understanding is there.“Yes, we have played enough cricket here in India; we all know the conditions, how to play, how to adjust ourselves, and we have played a series here against India, and the T20 World Cup, and the 50-over World Cup as well. We know the conditions really well, and how to play. We just need to execute the plan really well, according to the opposition, and that's it."Afghanistan eye first series win over IndiaAfghanistan are yet to beat India in a bilateral T20I series and Zadran is hoping his side can change that this time.He said the key will be to execute their plans properly and focus on the process instead of worrying about the result."Yes, we have played better cricket against India. In 2024, we had two super overs against them in the T20I series in Bengaluru.“At the ICC events, we have played better cricket against them. As you mentioned, we have never beaten them. Hopefully, we are going to play a good series, win a game, and win a series from them. But it's all about execution of the plan and giving your 100 percent.“It’s about trying to make things easy for ourselves, not complicated. Yes, we just try to give 100 percent. Don't think about the result; just try to think about the process, and how we are going to deliver. I am sure we will have a better series."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘We need to sit down and reflect on our mistakes’: Babar Azam calls for changes after Pakistan’s 0-3 England sweep
articles.summary: Cricket News: Pakistan captain Babar Azam has called for an honest assessment of the team's mistakes and selection strategy after England completed a 3-0 Test serie.
articles.body: Pakistan captain Babar Azam has called for an honest assessment of the team's mistakes and selection strategy after England completed a 3-0 Test series sweep with an eight-wicket victory at Edgbaston on Saturday.Babar admitted Pakistan now need to reassess their personnel and decide on their best playing XI after a difficult tour in which the visitors struggled to adapt to English conditions. He said the team management, selectors and captain would need to sit together and determine the way forward.“I think we need to sit down and reflect on our mistakes, decide what type of playing eleven, and decide our players. I think they are sitting, and the manager is coming, the selector is coming, and I sit back and then decide our best eleven,” Babar said after the defeat.The series ended with Pakistan's batting showing signs of improvement in Birmingham. After being bowled out for under 200 in both innings of the opening two Tests, they posted 449 in their second innings at Edgbaston to set England a target of 130.‘Unfortunately, we have a couple of changes after losing two matches’Debutant Razaullah provided the biggest spark for Pakistan, making an immediate impact with both bat and ball. He took four wickets in England's first innings before smashing 81 off 63 balls, including nine sixes.Shan Masood scored 95, Babar contributed 76 and opener Azam Awais made 59 as Pakistan finally offered substantial resistance with the bat.Mohammad Abbas then gave the visitors a glimmer of hope by removing two England batters in the opening over of England's chase. Babar admitted Pakistan briefly believed they could force an unlikely result before Joe Root and Jordan Cox took control.“Yes. We took two wickets in the first over. So we believe high, always high. But I think Root and both batsmen playing are very good,” he said.Root finished unbeaten on 62 and Cox scored 59, with their unbroken 128-run partnership taking England to victory.Reflecting on Pakistan's selection throughout the series, Babar described the changes made after the first two defeats as unfortunate, while also pointing to the difficulty of batting in the conditions.“Before we come here, we think about different things, and then we decide our team. And then unfortunately, we have a couple of changes after losing two matches because when we are coming to England, it is very difficult for the batsmen, and the first two pitches are very difficult,” he said.Babar backs Razaullah after breakthrough TestWhile Pakistan leave England with plenty to reconsider, Razaullah's performance offered a major positive. Despite his limited first-class experience, the youngster made an immediate impression on Test debut.“We enjoyed it. I think everyone is enjoying his innings and bowling, and he is a very good talent and raw. I think he’s good for us. However, the first T20I against Afghanistan here on Sunday will be the first time he can boast of having a first-choice team to work with.Iyer’s captaincy came in bizarre circumstances after the selectors decided to unceremoniously dump T20 World Cup-winning captain Suryakumar Yadav. We need to understand the amount of matches a player is playing continuously. He’s bound to get injured some way or the other because the intensity is pretty high,” Iyer said. “Of course, it certainly impacts the combination. All you can control is whoever is available on that given day, and we need to give that sort of confidence to that particular player. A backup is equally important for the team. We know they can deliver as well,” he added.This will also be the first time Iyer will have the services of pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah, who is coming off a long layoff. “As a player comes out of injury, it’s important that he gets more game time. Bumrah has played so much cricket over the years. articles.title: Diamondbacks 2, Texas 6: Return of the One Big Inning
articles.summary: At least Tim Tawa got his first major league triple, and Pavin Smith had an RBI!
articles.body:
Well, you know what they say: "You can't win 'em all." On paper, it looked like maybe we should have won this one, and if you were keeping score, it would not have been lost at you that we basically won eight out of the nine innings that were played tonight. Sadly, however, that's not how baseball works. Early in the season, before his forced vacation in Reno, we became very familiar with Brandon Pfaadt , tonight's starter, pitching at least okay for a handful of innings and then having there be the One Big Inning™ where everything kinda blew up. Upon Brandon's return, we still saw some of that, except that the offending innings were generally pretty mild—one or two or three runs at most, which kept things close enough that we could get back into it. But that was not the case tonight.

He was going up against former first-round draft pick and general underperformer Kumar Rocker , and in terms of the numbers, it was a very favorable matchup. Rocker is often wild, and throws a bunch of pitches, and gives up a lot of walks, and leaves ballgames a lot earlier than you tend to want your starter to leave. Irritatingly, though, he was quite efficient in the early going tonight, as he and Pfaadt traded quick, scoreless innings in the first and second. After two innings, Rocker had thrown 24 pitches; Pfaadt, despite having given up two hits to Rocker's none, had only thrown 23. Pfaadt had another shutdown inning in the top of the third, adding only 12 more pitches to his count and setting down the Rangers in order, and Tim Tawa led off the bottom of the third with a triple off the wall in pretty much straightaway center field:

Pavin Smith , who was for many of us a surprise call-up from Reno today, then grounded a single past Corey Seager and into left field to drive in Timmy. Three quick outs followed, but we'd drawn first blood against Rocker and that Rangers. 1-0 DBACKS

Pfaadt recorded another 1-2-3 inning in the top of the fourth, we sat down in order against Rocker in the bottom half, and then the fifth inning rolled around, much like a giant stone boulder bearing down a steep slope in a narrow passageway, heading straight for our guy. And alas, Brandon Pfgaadt was no Indiana Jones; he couldn't get out of the way.

It started with a leadoff dinger by Wyatt Langford to tie the game, and was followed by a single, a stoledn abse, a sacrifice bunt, another single that scored a run, a hit by pitch. and then a fielder's choice that looked like an inning-ending double play but which was overturned by a review that determined that Brandon Pfaadt's foot was perhaps not on the bag when he ran over to cover first base. The call on the field was "safe," and while the replays we saw on the broadcast really looked like they'd be enough to overturn that call, but it was not to be, and the call stood. That completely knocked Pfaadt off kilter, and the next three batters went single-double-single before he finally struck out Wyatt Langford, the tenth batter of the inning, to put it to bed. 6-1 Texas

And that was pretty much that. Somewhat surprisingly, Pfaadt came out and pitched the sixth, and he even recorded the first two outs in the seventh, and it was all good and all zeros, but the damage had been done.

Kumar Rocker, meanwhile, walked Nolan Arenado and Tim Tawa to lead off the bottom of the fifth, and that ended his night, and Texas got their bullpen involved and that bullpen also proved to be irritatingly effective. Both of the leadoff walks were left stranded. Rangers' opening day starter Nathan Eovaldi , fresh off the IL and returning to big league action without any rehab starts or anything, let us get a second run in the bottom of the sixth, thanks to one-out singles by Gabriel Moreno and Geraldo Perdomo , followed by a Corbin Carroll sacrifice fly that scored Moreno from third, which narrowed the game to 6-2 Texas

But that was where it stayed. Jonathan Loaisiga , Derek Law , and Juan Morillo put zeroes up the rest of the way for us, but there was nothing further doing from the offense, despite us putting the leadoff runners on in both the seventh and eighth innings. And so it was. 6-2 Texas FINAL

Loss Probability Added, courtesy of FanGraphs

The Lost Ark: Nobody . The Last Crusade: Tim Tawa (3 AB, 1 H, 1 R, 1 3B, 1 BB, +10% WPA) The Crystal Skull: Brandon Pfaadt (6 2/3 IP, 10 H, 6 R, 6 ER, 0 BB, 7 K, 1 HR, -34% WPA)

It was a fairly sparse Gameday Thread this evening, with 201 comments at time of writing. Precious few recs got handed out tonight as well, and pretty much the only comments to go Sedona Red were concentrated at the start of the game, when folks were still marveling at the return of Pavin Smith to a major league roster and a starting lineup. As such, tonight's Comment of the Game goes to onedotfive, for this solid suggestion about how we might find a way to turn his presence to our collective advantage in the remaining days of the season:

Works for me….I think Baxter is creepy anyway.

So join us tomorrow afternoon for the rubber match of the series. Hologram Eddie takes the mound for us; Cal Quantrill goes for Texas. First pitch is scheduled for 1:10pm AZ time. Hope to see you around the place!

As always, thanks for reading, and as always, go Diamondbacks !

articles.title: Will India accept the Women's Asia Cup trophy from Mohsin Naqvi? Exploring possible boycott of Pakistan's ACC and PCB chief
articles.summary: With Pakistan Cricket Board Chief Mohsin Naqvi set to present the Asia Cup to the winning team, here's if Team India Women will accept the trophy from him.
articles.body:
The Men's Asia Cup trophy still has not been handed over to India after the September 2025 final.

Mohsin Naqvi is expected to attend the Women's Asia Cup final in Dubai on September 13.

India's men refused to accept the trophy from Naqvi, who is also Pakistan's interior minister.

Will India accept the Women's Asia Cup trophy from Mohsin Naqvi?

India's women are the side to be defeated at the 2026 Asia Cup and the clear favourites to reach the final on September 13. However, one question remains that has nothing to do with cricket. If Harmanpreet Kaur's team lifts the trophy, who will hand it to them?

Under normal circumstances, the answer would be the president of the Asian Cricket Council. That happens to be Mohsin Naqvi, who is simultaneously the chairman of the Pakistan Cricket Board and the interior minister of Pakistan, a combination of roles that caused a full-blown diplomatic incident the last time he tried to present a trophy to an Indian side.

Journalist Rohit Jaglan of Rezsports flagged the issue ahead of the group stage, noting that Naqvi was not present for the Women's Asia Cup trophy unveiling ceremony but had attended the corresponding men's event. His absence from the unveiling does not guarantee his absence from the final.

Who is Mohsin Naqvi, and why would he present the Women's Asia Cup trophy?

Naqvi was elected ACC president for a two-year term in April 2025, succeeding Sri Lanka's Shammi Silva. He holds the position alongside his PCB chairmanship and his cabinet portfolio as Pakistan's interior minister, a combination that has made him arguably the most politically prominent figure in Asian cricket administration.

His path to the cricket establishment began through politics rather than the sport itself. Naqvi served as caretaker chief minister of Punjab province from January 2023 to February 2024, and his appointment to the PCB came without a professional cricketing background.

He has since consolidated his position, with PCB-backed candidates sweeping all three contested ACC board seats at the Bangkok AGM in August 2026.

As ACC president, it is his prerogative to present the trophy at the continental body's flagship events. He did so at the Men's Asia Cup final in September 2025, or at least attempted to, and was listed in the ACC's official pre-tournament communication as the individual who would hand over the silverware to the winners.

What happened when India's men's team refused to accept the trophy from Naqvi?

India beat Pakistan by five wickets in a thrilling final-over finish at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium on September 28, 2025. What followed was one of the most extraordinary episodes in Asian cricket's history.

The presentation ceremony was delayed by more than an hour after the match ended. While the match finished at around 10:30 PM Dubai time, the wait stretched to close to midnight. BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia confirmed what had caused the hold-up.

"We have decided not to take the Asia Cup trophy from the ACC chairman, who happens to be one of the main political leaders of Pakistan," Saikia told ANI. "So we decided not to take it from him."

India's players had reportedly indicated they were willing to accept the trophy from Emirates Cricket Board vice-chairman Khalid Al Zarooni instead, but that request was denied. Eventually, an official quietly removed the trophy from the dais and carried it off the field without explanation.

Suryakumar Yadav's team celebrated their victory without the physical trophy, posing for photographs miming the act of holding it. The standoff reflected the broader political tensions between the two countries following the Pahalgam terror attack in April 2025, which had already seen India refuse to shake hands with Pakistan players across all three meetings during the tournament.

The trophy still had not reached the BCCI by early November. Saikia wrote to the ACC requesting its handover, and when Naqvi refused to release it, the BCCI threatened to raise the matter at the ICC meeting on November 4. Naqvi denied having apologised and instead invited India to collect the trophy from the ACC office in Dubai.

Will India captain, Harmanpreet Kaur, accept the trophy if they win the Women's Asia Cup?

No official position has been stated by the BCCI on the women's tournament, and the question has not been put directly to Harmanpreet Kaur or the team management. It is, however, impossible to separate it from the unresolved men's trophy standoff.

There are three possible outcomes if India reaches the final and wins. The first is that Naqvi presents the trophy and India accepts it, which would represent a climbdown from the position Saikia articulated in September and seems unlikely given the men's trophy dispute remains open.

The second is a repeat of the men's scenario, with India refusing and the ceremony descending into another standoff at the same venue. The third, and perhaps likeliest, is that the ACC quietly arranges for a different dignitary to handle the presentation, avoiding the confrontation entirely.

Naqvi's absence from the trophy unveiling ceremony may hint at this kind of behind-the-scenes arrangement, though nothing has been confirmed. What is certain is that this is not a decision the players will make on their own.

If the men's episode demonstrated anything, it was that the instruction came from the BCCI rather than the dressing room, and any directive for the women's final will follow the same chain. The players will play the cricket, the board will handle the politics, and whether the trophy ends up in their hands or in the ACC office will be determined well above Harmanpreet Kaur's pay grade.

articles.title: ‘I’d be open to it’: Mike Hesson eyes Pakistan Test role as Shaheen Afridi makes red-ball return
articles.summary: Cricket News: Mike Hesson has opened the door to a permanent role as Pakistan’s Test coach after stepping in for the third Test in the team’s 0-3 series whitewash a.
articles.body: Mike Hesson has opened the door to a permanent role as Pakistan’s Test coach after stepping in for the third Test in the team’s 0-3 series whitewash against England, while Shaheen Shah Afridi has made his own intentions clear by declaring that red-ball cricket remains his “first priority”.Hesson, who was handed interim charge of Pakistan’s Test side after the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) removed Sarfaraz Ahmed following the defeat at Lord’s, admitted he would be interested in continuing with the red-ball setup.“I’d be open to it, for sure,” Hesson said at the post-match press conference.The New Zealander had initially made it clear that his Test coaching assignment was temporary. But after Pakistan’s eight-wicket defeat at Edgbaston completed England’s 3-0 series sweep, Hesson suggested he sees enough potential in the squad to consider taking on the responsibility permanently.Hesson sees talent in Pakistan's Test setupHesson said Pakistan have enough ability within their Test system to make progress, although he acknowledged that rebuilding the side would require time and direction.“I love Test cricket, and there’s enough talent around the system in Pakistan that if we provide some good direction, we can make some strides going forward. It’s not going to happen in a game or two, but there’s some skill there I’d certainly be considering looking after,” he said.However, Hesson stressed that any decision on his future would involve the PCB and selectors. His immediate focus remains Pakistan’s white-ball commitments, particularly the Asian Games.“I haven’t even contemplated [a job offer] at this stage. I’ve got the Asian Games coming a week after I get back. That’s my main focus in terms of the white ball. By the time that arrives, I’m sure we’ll have some discussions about the Test team going forward. That’s a discussion I’ll have with the selectors,” he said.Pakistan's Test campaign ended on a disappointing note despite a spirited second-innings fightback.Afridi makes red-ball priority clearAs Pakistan look to rebuild their Test side, Afridi’s return to first-class cricket could provide a significant boost. The left-arm pacer featured in the President’s Trophy on Saturday, making his first competitive domestic red-ball appearance since 2019.“Red-ball cricket is always my first priority,” Afridi said, as per the ICC website.“I’ve always loved it. I didn’t get enough time to play because of international cricket, but I haven’t been playing much cricket for the last couple of months. So it’s an opportunity to play red-ball cricket,” he added.Afridi, who has 126 wickets in 34 Tests, was left out of Pakistan’s squads for the West Indies and England tours. He said returning to longer-format cricket would help sharpen his rhythm and confidence.“I learned a lot from my elder brother Riaz Afridi, because he’s played a lot of first-class cricket,” he said. “In the longer format, the longer you spend time on the ground (the better it is) for your confidence, and for your line and length to get fine-tuned.”‘When you’re free, you should play domestic cricket’Afridi also acknowledged the difficulty of switching between formats after spending much of his career on an intense international schedule.“I’ve not played red-ball cricket for the last few months. Before that, I’d been playing red-ball cricket continuously,” he said.“If you play international cricket, then coming back to domestic cricket can be challenging. Because you’ve been playing international cricket constantly in all three formats, it keeps you busy. When you’re free, you should play domestic cricket.”The pacer said he would not alter his approach with the ball in first-class cricket.“I’ll try to bowl the same way in first-class cricket as I’ve bowled in Test cricket,” Afridi said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Mohammed Shami’s chances of returning to international cricket for India appear uncertain, with the pacer having not played for the national team for one-and-a-half years. Now 36, Shami has dealt with recurring injuries in recent years, and the Ajit Agarkar-led BCCI selection committee appears to have moved towards a younger group of fast bowlers.This has led to questions over whether Shami is being overlooked because of his age, especially as he has continued to perform in domestic cricket. There have been arguments that the BCCI should not rule him out because of his age, pointing to experienced fast bowlers such as Mitchell Starc, who continue to play for Australia.However, former India cricketer Aakash Chopra said age is not the only reason Shami is out of the Indian team."There is a stark difference between Mohammed Shami and Mitchell Starc. Starc has remained fit and played continuously, and whenever he has returned to action, he has spearheaded the (Australian) attack. No question can be raised over his form, fitness and sharpness," Chopra said, in a video posted by CREX."Mohammed Shami, on the other hand, has had injuries. He had a surgery and then spent time out of action. When he returned to domestic cricket, there were question marks over his pace and whether he was in full swing. He did take wickets, but that intensity appeared to be lacking," he said.Chopra also rejected the idea that Shami’s age is the reason he has been left out, pointing to the continued selection of Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma, who are older than Shami."Is Shami's age going against him? I think that would be preposterous. It makes no sense whatsoever to drop someone because of his age, because you are still selecting veterans like Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma.""I don't think age is the factor. At some point, the selectors will spell out the reason, but I don't think it is age," Chopra concluded.Shami recently completed 100 first-class matches after playing for East Zone in the Duleep Trophy 2026 final.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ranji Trophy: Brabourne Stadium to be Railways home venue in 2026-27 season
articles.summary: Cricket News: MUMBAI: In a first, the iconic Brabourne Stadium at the Cricket Club of India here will be the home venue of Railways in the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy.In t.
articles.body: MUMBAI: In a first, the iconic Brabourne Stadium at the Cricket Club of India here will be the home venue of Railways in the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy.In the past, the Railways have played their home Ranji Trophy matches at the Karnail Singh Stadium in New Delhi.Placed in Elite Group D, Railways will play their three 2026-27 Ranji Trophy home ties at the Brabourne Stadium-their season-the opening match against Uttarakhand from Oct 11-14, the big game against 42-time champions Mumbai (it will be an away game for Mumbai!) from Nov 2-5, and then against Haryana from Jan 17-20.This will be the first time the Brabourne Stadium will stage a Ranji Trophy match in more than three years. The historic venue last staged a Ranji Trophy match between Mumbai and Maharashtra from Jan 24-27, 2023. The match ended in a draw."I'm truly happy that the Ranji Trophy is returning to the CCI. The Brabourne Stadium has staged the maximum number of Ranji Trophy finals (16) in India. There's a replica of the Ranji Trophy in the CCI main hall, which was kept by former BCCI and CCI president Raj Singh Dungarpur many years back. So, there has always been a special and cherished relationship between Brabourne stadium CCI's senior member and well-known cricket lover Sachin Bajaj told TOI on Saturday."My old friend Syed Zakaria Zuffri (former Assam and Railways ‘keeper-batsman and current Railways head coach) requested to me if the CCI could stage Railways' home Ranji Trophy matches in the upcoming season. I asked him to contact CCI's Cricket committee vice-chairman Mayank Khandwala in this regard. I must appreciate the efforts of Mayank and the CCI cricket committee in making this happen," he added."It is a matter of immense pride and great emotion for all of us at the Cricket Club of India to welcome the Ranji Trophy back to Brabourne Stadium after a significant interval. Cricket at CCI is not merely a sport, it is part of the Club’s identity, its heritage and its soul. For generations, Brabourne Stadium has witnessed some of the finest moments in Indian cricket and has been privileged to host legendary players, great teams and memorable encounters. The Ranji Trophy has always held a very special place in that extraordinary history. The return of first-class cricket to CCI is therefore much more than the staging of a few matches. It is the revival of a proud cricketing tradition and the reopening of a historic chapter. We are particularly delighted that Railways have chosen CCI as their home ground. We are honoured to partner with them and are committed to providing the players, officials and spectators with the very best facilities and an environment befitting the stature of the Ranji Trophy," Khandwala told TOI."As the vice-chairman of the Cricket Committee at CCI, I believe strongly that our responsibility is not only to preserve the magnificent cricketing legacy of this institution, but also to keep that legacy alive for the next generation. Bringing premier domestic cricket back to Brabourne is an important part of that vision. The Ranji Trophy represents the foundation of Indian cricket. It is where talent is tested, characters are built and future international stars begin their journey. To have that journey once again unfolding at CCI is something we should all celebrate. The Brabourne Stadium has a history that speaks for itself. Now, we look forward to creating the next chapter. On behalf of CCI, we extend a warm welcome to Railways, the players, support staff, match officials, the BCCI and, most importantly, cricket lovers who will return to CCI to experience the magic of first-class cricket. The Ranji Trophy is coming home to CCI. The heritage continues, and the next chapter begins," he added.The Railways team playing its home ties in the Ranji Trophy in the upcoming season is another step forward in cricket returning to CCI. articles.title: ‘A very unusual summer’: England’s Ben Stokes retirement, McCullum exit, Carse controversy and Root’s return end in 3-0 Pakistan sweep
articles.summary: Cricket News: England have emerged from a summer of upheaval with a perfect 3-0 Test series sweep against Pakistan, and returning captain Joe Root believes the way .
articles.body: England have emerged from a summer of upheaval with a perfect 3-0 Test series sweep against Pakistan, and returning captain Joe Root believes the way his side responded to an “unusual” period of change has been particularly encouraging.Root returned to the Test captaincy after Ben Stokes retired from international cricket, while former New Zealand batter Stephen Fleming was appointed as England’s new head coach following Brendon McCullum’s departure after four years.There were also off-field distractions, including fast bowler Brydon Carse being dropped from the England squad following an incident outside a nightclub in Derby.Despite the turbulence, England completed a convincing eight-wicket victory in the third Test at Edgbaston on Saturday to seal a 3-0 series sweep.“There’s been a lot of chaos around this series before a ball was bowled,” Root said at the post-match press conference. “At the start of the series, we wanted 3-0 and we’ve been clinical enough to do that.”‘It’s been a very unusual summer’Root, 35, who is the second-highest run-scorer in Test history, admitted the changes and controversies had made for an unusual summer for England.“It’s been a very unusual summer, hasn’t it? That’s probably a better way of putting it. There’s been a lot of different things happen. We had a resignation mid-series, there has been a few off-field incidents and we’ve got a new coach,” he said.“Whether you call it chaos, whether you call it unusual, whether you call it unsettling, all are fair. But ultimately, the thing that I care about, and that’s most important, is what happens from that. And I think the way that we’ve responded to that has been excellent.”Root added that the side now has greater clarity over its direction.“And the fact that there’s now clarity in what is expected of the group moving forward is quite evident and we build on that now,” he said.Root credits Stokes and McCullumWhile back at the helm, Root was quick to acknowledge that England’s success remains rooted in the transformation overseen by Stokes and McCullum.“I don’t think we would have been able to play in the manner that we have without the work that Brendon (McCullum) did as coach and Ben (Stokes) as captain. And I think it’s a continuation and a small evolution of all the stuff that happened before this,” Root said.“So that has to continue forward, and we’ll continue to keep trying to evolve that and improve on what’s been a really good summer here,” he added.England’s ability to handle pressure was tested in the third Test after Pakistan mounted a strong second-innings fightback. Pakistan scored 449 after being dismissed for 133 in the first innings, with Shan Masood making 95, Babar Azam 76 and debutant Razaullah hitting 81.But England chased 130 comfortably, with Root unbeaten on 62 and Jordan Cox making 59 in an unbroken 128-run partnership.“We’ve had things go our own way a little bit throughout the series, and we had a little bit of pushback yesterday, which was, in a strange way, quite a good thing for the group,” Root said.“But for us to come through it and be so convincing in the way that we’ve finished the series off, and throughout the whole three games really, has been really pleasing,” he added.Praise for Razaullah and TrescothickRoot also singled out Pakistan debutant Razaullah, who struck nine sixes in his 63-ball 81.“He played some wonderful shots, made it quite difficult to set fields to, and struck the ball nicely. I don’t know how he’s not pulled a side really; he’s swinging that hard. But fair play, he played nicely and made it difficult for us,” Root said.The England captain also praised interim coach Marcus Trescothick for guiding the side through the transition.“I think he’s been awesome. It can’t be an easy thing when you know that it’s not a long-term role,” Root said.“For him to be able to sort of juggle between trying to look forward and what that might look like, but also be able to have his influence and his way of seeing the game on this group has been fantastic,” he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: England player ratings for third Test at Edgbaston: Dan Lawrence, Jordan Cox and Emilio Gay add to selection headache
articles.summary: Dan Lawrence earns Player of the Match honours at Edgbaston after hitting fifty, taking two wickets and claiming a stunning slip catch; Emilio Gay and Jordan Cox also hit half-centuries, with the trio tussling for a permanent place in the Test team as England sweep series against Pakistan
articles.body:
A Test match to forget for Duckett. In fact, it has been a pretty miserable series as a whole, with his first-innings 17 at Lord's serving as his highest score.

He did, however, notch England's only Test ton of the summer against New Zealand at Trent Bridge, so his place at the top of the order isn't under threat - at least for now...

He was also a bit butter-fingered in the slips this week, dropping three chances, albeit his two put down in the first innings didn't prove too costly as Pakistan were still bundled out for 133 in only 33.5 overs.

It has been a bit of a back-and-forth affair with regards to Gay's place in the starting Test side going forward, with the Durham left-hander seemingly locking up his spot with another battling half-century in the first innings - his third such score this summer.

But then his second-innings duck has somewhat opened up the debate again, especially given the performance of others who could end up elbowing him out of the way when the currently injured Jacob Bethell likely returns to the team.

It was, admittedly, a terrific delivery from Mohammad Abbas that ensured he wouldn't trouble the scorers in the second innings, but it's precisely why he'll be kicking himself with how he got out first time round - dragging a wide one from Razaullah back onto his stumps - when a first Test hundred was there for the taking.

Much like Gay, Cox's fortunes and future prospects see-sawed a touch over the course of this Test, as he copped a low one in the first innings - also falling foul of Abbas, lbw - but his calm, unbeaten half-century alongside the skipper on the fourth morning saw England to victory from a positon of peril at 2-2.

It will have been hard for Joe Root not to have taken note of that, as he looks for the right sort of characters to take this side forward. And Cox seems to have character in spades.

That was also evident with his keeping, when deputising impressively for Jamie Smith, who sat out the second innings with an injured thumb. He claimed four terrific catches and a stumping to finally end Razaullah's extraordinary knock.

Just when England needed a captain's innings, Root duly obliged, his unbeaten half-century on the fourth morning - just his third of a barren summer by his standards - allaying any fears of a catastrophic late collapse to defeat.

Instead, he celebrates a series sweep - England's first at home over Pakistan - on his return as permanent Test captain, though his lbw issues persist after Razaullah was the one to pin him in the first innings, in spectacular fashion with only his fourth ball in Test cricket. It takes Root's tally to eight such dismissals from his 10 Test innings' this summer.

Also, he moved one clear of Australia's Steve Smith and onto 220 in their personal battle to claim the record number of catches by an outfielder in Test cricket.

Brook will be another kicking himself for missing out on a hundred in the first innings, with one seemingly at his mercy before he needlessly ran himself out on the second morning.

He's been England's most consistent batter in the testing conditions served up this summer, with this his fifth half-century, while he has had starts of at least 20 in all but two of his innings.

It will make him all the more frustrated at the fact that a century has eluded him, but he has shown greater responsibility with the bat - certainly against Pakistan - which is encouraging after fans began growing tired of his, at times, reckless approach in the Bazball era.

Player of the match. With Ollie Robinson denied for the first time in a Test he's played this summer.

Lawrence is another vying for a regular place in this side and he's certainly done his chances no harm, with bat, ball and in the field.

His standout contribution was a spectacular catch in the slips - one-handed, diving low to his right - to see off Shan Masood five shy of a century. But he also grabbed two wickets in his 4.4 second-innings overs, including Azan Awais (59) to end his 125-run third-wicket stand with Masood and finally the wicket of Razaullah to end day three.

If anything his off-spin was under-used, with that being a key string to his bow to support England's preference for a four-pronged pace attack looking ahead to the winter tour of South Africa and next summer's Ashes.

With the bat, like Gay and Brook before him, he'll rue missing out on a first-innings ton when dragging a rather innocuous delivery from Mohammad Imran back onto his stumps.

The forgotten man in this Test, with his involvement ended two days in, as a blow to the finger when stood up to the stumps on day one prevented him from donning the gloves in the second innings.

It looks a precautionary measure more than anything, with it not keeping him from batting on day two as he again impressed with a typically brisk 69 before chipping one back to Razaullah off his own bowling.

While Cox impressed in his absence, Smith has also barely put a foot wrong behind the stumps all summer, so he'll likely still start if fit for South Africa.

It's been tough sledding for Atkinson this series, with only one wicket to show for his efforts prior to the second innings - as the rest of the pace quartet profited.

He has bowled better than his numbers would suggest, often coming on as second change, sidelined as others wreaked havoc with the new ball and when bowling to the tail.

But Root showed faith in his fast bowler after lunch on day three, with Pakistan 184-3 in their second innings, letting him loose for an eight-over spell that was his best yet and brought with it the wicket of Masood - as much as he owed a debt of gratitude to Lawrence too.

He'd later add Ghazi Ghori and Imran before he too couldn't escape punishment from the blade of Razaullah.

Robinson was at it yet again with the new ball, dismissing Saim Ayub and Abdullah Shafique in his opening spell in both innings, needing only four deliveries to see the back of them second time round - the former out for a pair upon his sudden, surprise call up to the touring side in between Tests that did him no favours.

Robinson's wicket of Saim in the first innings was his 100th in Test cricket, while his double strike in the first over of the second took his tally for the series to 21 at an average of 6.66 a pop, which grew to just the 8.76 apiece upon Pakistan's battling display on day three.

In all seriousness, his effectiveness does diminish when taken deep into later spells, which could be a concern on flatter decks if that's what awaits in South Africa or next year's Ashes, but it's extremely hard to pick fault given just how impressive his reintroduction to the side has been this summer.

Also pitched in with the bat, scoring his second Test fifty.

Not his best showing, with at least one of his three first-innings wickets a real gift from Masood, spooned straight to midwicket.

His dismissal of Saud Shakeel to a brute of a short ball in the second gave nod to him at his best, but he was one of several England bowlers to lose the plot late on the third evening as Razaullah smacked them to all parts.

Still, an encouraging summer on the whole, with five consecutive Tests for the previously injury-plagued pacer a real tick for England.

Trademark Tongue in the first innings, with three of his four wickets scattering the stumps - the top of Babar's off peg knocked back with the fast bowler's dream delivery, Imran undone by a toe-crushing yorker and Shakeel seen off by a devastating nip-backer.

He was expensive in the second innings, going at more than six an over, until his and Archer's bouncer theory proved incisive - until Razaullah arrived at the middle, that is - as Tongue got Babar to glove one behind.

Third Test (Edgbaston) - England won by eight wickets

articles.title: Women’s Asia Cup: Nigar Sultana’s handshake snub to Harmanpreet Kaur backfires as BCB distances itself, puts captaincy under review
articles.summary: Cricket News: Bangladesh captain Nigar Sultana’s decision to skip the traditional handshake with India skipper Harmanpreet Kaur at the toss of the Women’s Asia Cup .
articles.body: Bangladesh captain Nigar Sultana’s decision to skip the traditional handshake with India skipper Harmanpreet Kaur at the toss of the Women’s Asia Cup semi-final has left her own cricket board distancing itself from the gesture.The incident came before Bangladesh’s 40-run defeat to India, with Nigar refusing to shake hands with Harmanpreet during the pre-match proceedings. While the move immediately drew attention amid the recent tensions surrounding handshakes in India-Pakistan cricket, the Bangladesh Cricket Board made it clear that the captain’s decision was not sanctioned by the board.Rafiqul Islam Babu, chairman of the BCB women's committee, said Nigar acted on her own and insisted that the board remained committed to maintaining cordial relations with all cricketing nations.“Of course, it was her own decision (not to shake hands with Harmanpreet),” Babu said. “We believe sports bring the world together. We want friendly relations with all countries, not just India and so whatever she did was entirely her personal decision.”BCB distances itself from Nigar’s decisionThe clarification from Babu effectively ruled out any suggestion that Bangladesh had adopted a broader no-handshake policy similar to the one seen in recent India-Pakistan men’s fixtures.Nigar’s decision came against the backdrop of heightened political tensions between India and Pakistan, which had spilled over into cricket after last year’s men’s Asia Cup. Indian captains had subsequently avoided handshakes with their Pakistani counterparts, making the Bangladesh skipper’s gesture particularly noticeable when she followed a similar route against India.However, BCB has stressed that there was no board directive behind Nigar’s decision.The focus now appears to have shifted from the toss incident to the captain’s future, with the board confirming that her position will be assessed after the Asian Games.Nigar’s captaincy under reviewBabu revealed that complaints had also been lodged against Nigar over alleged misconduct, adding another layer of uncertainty around her leadership.“We have discussed the thing (performance and complaint) in total with the board president and since they are in Asian Games we will assess the situation after the conclusion of the games,” he said.“First, we will see how the team performs at the Asian Games, then decide what needs to be done,” Babu added.The comments suggest that Nigar’s future will be determined not by the controversy surrounding the handshake, but by Bangladesh’s performances and the complaints made against her.Bangladesh fall short against IndiaOn the field, Bangladesh were unable to match India in the semi-final. Chasing 150, they were bowled out for a 40-run defeat, ending their campaign and sending India into the final.Babu acknowledged that Bangladesh continue to struggle against the stronger sides despite showing signs of improvement.“There are many shortcomings in the team. We have not been able to beat the bigger teams. We played well in the World Cup too but lost because of small mistakes,” he said.“We are working to make the team stronger and more competitive. After the Asian Games we will decide what can be done,” he concluded.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Why India are playing as 'away' team in Delhi for Afghanistan T20I series: Explained
articles.summary: Cricket News: India will begin their three-match T20I series against Afghanistan with the first match at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in Delhi on Sunday. While the matc.
articles.body: India will begin their three-match T20I series against Afghanistan with the first match at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in Delhi on Sunday. While the match is being played in India, the series is officially a home series for Afghanistan.The Afghanistan Cricket Board is hosting all three T20Is in Delhi, with the remaining two matches also scheduled at the same venue. Both teams are using the series to prepare for the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya.Why India are the away team in DelhiEven though the matches are being played in Delhi, India will take the field as the visiting team because Afghanistan are the designated hosts of the series.For security reasons, Afghanistan cannot host international matches in their own country. As a result, they play their home fixtures in India or the UAE. Afghanistan have hosted other international teams in India before, but this is the first time they are hosting India on Indian soil.It will also be a first for Indian cricket. In the 94-year history of Indian cricket, this is the first time India will play a match at home without being the home team.Afghanistan captain will toss the coinAs the home side, Afghanistan captain Ibrahim Zadran will toss the coin before the match, while India captain Shreyas Iyer will call heads or tails.India to use the away dressing roomThe Arun Jaitley Stadium has separate dressing rooms for the home and visiting teams. For this series, Afghanistan will use the home dressing room, while India will use the visitors’ dressing room.The series also gives the Afghanistan Cricket Board an opportunity to earn revenue from broadcast rights, ticket sales and in-stadium commercial rights through a “home away from home” series in India.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Joe Root achieves what no batter has done in 147 years of Test cricket, becomes first batter to score 2,000 fourth-innings runs
articles.summary: Cricket News: Joe Root has added another extraordinary record to his already remarkable Test career, becoming the first player in the 147-year history of Test crick.
articles.body: Joe Root has added another extraordinary record to his already remarkable Test career, becoming the first player in the 147-year history of Test cricket to cross the 2,000-run mark specifically in the fourth innings. The England star reached the landmark during his unbeaten 62 against Pakistan in the third Test at Edgbaston, producing yet another defining contribution when his team needed him most.Fourth-innings batting is arguably the ultimate examination of a Test batter. The pitch is often at its most challenging, the target is on the scoreboard and every wicket brings the chasing team closer to defeat.Root has made that pressure situation his own.Batter4th Innings Test RunsJoe Root (ENG)2,059Sachin Tendulkar (IND)1,625Alastair Cook (ENG)1,611Graeme Smith (RSA)1,611Shivnarine Chanderpaul (WI)1,580Root's fourth-innings dominance reaches another levelRoot's historic achievement came during England's chase of 130 in the third and final Test against Pakistan. The hosts suffered a nightmare beginning, losing Ben Duckett and Emilio Gay in the opening over to slip to 2/2.With Pakistan suddenly sensing an opportunity to defend a modest target, Root walked into the middle with England under pressure. As has so often been the case throughout his career, the situation appeared to bring out the best in him.Root steadied the chase alongside Jordan Cox, eventually remaining unbeaten on 62 as England reached 130/2 and completed an eight-wicket victory. Cox also remained unbeaten on 59, with the pair putting together a match-winning partnership after England's early collapse.The victory completed a 3-0 Test series sweep for England, giving Root the perfect finish to his return to the Test captaincy.Root also becomes the first batter to score 1,000 runs at EdgbastonThe fourth-innings record was not the only piece of history Root created at Edgbaston. During the same innings, he became the first batter to score more than 1,000 Test runs at the Birmingham venue. Root had entered the match needing 52 runs to reach the landmark, having already accumulated 948 runs at Edgbaston.Edgbaston is now the fourth Test venue where Root has scored at least 1,000 runs.His other major haunts are:Lord's – 2,203 runsManchester – 1,128 runsThe Oval – 1,050 runsEdgbaston – 1,018 runsThat achievement places Root alongside Jacques Kallis and Ricky Ponting as only the third batter to score 1,000 or more Test runs at four different venues.And then came another record involving Sachin TendulkarRoot's 62 not out also produced another major milestone. The innings was his 69th Test fifty, moving him to the top of the all-time list for half-centuries. That took him past India's batting great Sachin Tendulkar, who finished his Test career with 68 fifties.Root now leads the list with 69, followed by Tendulkar on 68 and Shivnarine Chanderpaul on 66. Allan Border and Rahul Dravid have 63 each, while Ricky Ponting has 62. There is another remarkable aspect to that record: Root reached his 69 fifties in fewer Test innings than Tendulkar needed to reach 68.Root's 110th fifty-plus scoreThe 62 not out was also Root's 110th Test innings in which he scored at least 50 runs. That tally includes 41 centuries and 69 fifties, underlining just how consistently he has converted opportunities into substantial scores throughout his career. Reuters confirmed the Edgbaston innings as his 110th Test score of 50 or more.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'I don't cry for my real life': Smriti Mandhana's reply when asked when she last cried
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: India women's cricket team vice-captain Smriti Mandhana is one of the biggest names in women's cricket. Over the years, she has become one .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India women's cricket team vice-captain Smriti Mandhana is one of the biggest names in women's cricket. Over the years, she has become one of the key players for India and has inspired many young cricketers with her batting and leadership.However, while her cricket career has continued to grow, Mandhana has also gone through a difficult phase in her personal life. Her marriage was called off last year.Mandhana has not spoken publicly about Palash Muchhal, the man she was supposed to marry. During a recent podcast with Shamani, she was asked about the hardest night of her life.Mandhana took a long pause before making it clear that she wanted to speak only about cricket.Smriti Mandhana asked about the last time she criedDuring the conversation, Shamani asked Mandhana a direct question."When was the last time you cried??" Shamani asked.Mandhana appeared emotional and paused for several seconds before answering the question."Good question. I don't remember. You know, I cry for movies. I don't cry for my real life," Mandhana said.The India star then spoke about a movie that made her emotional."If I watch a movie, I cry. So I think I was watching Mosafir Cafe and it just got me emotional, happy emotional. And I cried," she said.Mandhana then explained why the movie made her emotional."It was very nice. Not even. I got very happy emotion. I was like, yeah, man. I also want to do something like just leave everything, just," she said.Smriti Mandhana's focus remains on cricketMandhana has largely stayed away from discussing her personal life in public after her marriage was called off.Even during the podcast, she chose to keep the conversation focused on her cricket journey when asked about the difficult period in her life.The India opener now faces another big challenge as India take on Sri Lanka in the Women's Asia Cup final in Dubai.Vivek Razdan wants Mandhana to play her natural gameFormer India men's cricketer Vivek Razdan believes Mandhana will be one of the most important players for India in the final.India enter Sunday's final as favourites, but defending champions Sri Lanka cannot be taken lightly after their comeback win over Pakistan in the semifinal."The Indian team is a very strong team. But you can't underestimate Sri Lanka, especially the way they played against Pakistan. After being 33/4, they chased down the required target. Despite Athapaththu being out early, you can see how much batting depth the team has," Razdan told IANS in a virtual interaction organised by Sony Sports Network.Razdan also praised India's bowling attack, which has played an important role in the tournament. He, however, wants Mandhana to focus on her own strengths instead of trying to match the aggressive approach of Shafali Verma.'Smriti sometimes tries to be Shafali'Shafali and Mandhana have been India's main run-scorers in the tournament so far, with 168 and 154 runs respectively.Razdan said India need to improve their batting in the powerplay and highlighted the importance of Mandhana staying at the crease for a long time."The Indian team bowling line-up is very strong. You can talk about N Sree Charni, Shafali, or Deepti. All of them have been very strong in these games. But there is one thing that needs to be worked on - how do you bat in powerplay?"In the last game, Shafali scored a fifty against Bangladesh, but she survived three dropped catches and one run-out chance. Regarding Smriti Mandhana, it is very important for her to play for a long time. I don't know why, but I feel that Smriti sometimes tries to be Shafali. That's not her game."Razdan's big expectation from MandhanaRazdan believes India can put up a big total if the top order avoids losing wickets early.With India's middle and lower order capable of finishing strongly, he feels Mandhana's role at the top could prove decisive on Dubai's slow pitches."If you can play the powerplay without losing a wicket, you will be able to post a big score because all of this depends on the top four. We have some batters who can help you at the back end. But if you want to win the match and the final, I will have a special eye on someone to do it, and it will be Smriti Mandhana."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: India captain Harmanpreet Kaur believes her team’s all-round progress throughout the Women’s T20 Asia Cup has given them the confidence to take on Sri Lanka in Sunday’s final at the Dubai International Stadium.India have been unbeaten in the tournament and will be determined to reclaim the continental crown after Sri Lanka defeated them in the 2024 final. With another title clash against the same opposition now on the horizon, Harmanpreet wants her side to stick to the basics rather than make any major changes.Harmanpreet backs India’s steady improvementIndia have continued to find ways to improve as the tournament has progressed, with Harmanpreet highlighting the team’s development in all three departments.“I think so far the tournament has been really, really good for us. We have seen massive improvement, whether it’s batting, bowling, or fielding, day by day. We’re getting used to these conditions and coming up with some really solid performances,” Harmanpreet said in a BCCI video.The captain believes adapting to the Dubai conditions has also helped India become more comfortable as the tournament has progressed.‘Nothing new, nothing different’ for IndiaWith a trophy at stake, Harmanpreet does not want her players to overcomplicate the occasion. Instead, the India skipper wants the team to trust the plans that have taken them to the final and approach the title clash with a positive mindset.“All set for the trophy. Hopefully, we’ll come up with some really positive approach,” she said.Harmanpreet later summed up her approach to the final simply: “Nothing new, nothing different, just sticking to our strength, to our plans and, at the same time, enjoying yourself on the field.”Experience giving Harmanpreet confidenceThe Asia Cup has also been a tournament of milestones for India, with Harmanpreet completing 150 matches as captain while Smriti Mandhana has also reached significant run-scoring landmarks.For Harmanpreet, the presence of experienced players throughout the squad has been a major source of confidence.“Every day we’re celebrating some great milestone, whether it’s Smriti’s runs or me representing the 150th game as a captain. So I think every day, it's good to see that so many girls are coming up with good performances and good milestones,” she said.“I think you need a team where you have so many members with so much experience. I think that gives me so much confidence, leading a side which has so many runs behind, wickets behind,” she added.India face fielding challenge in finalWhile India have been impressive overall, their fielding remains an area that needs attention. The team has dropped nine catches across four matches, a statistic that could prove costly against a Sri Lankan side that has already demonstrated its ability to fight under pressure.Sri Lanka produced a remarkable comeback in their semifinal against Pakistan, recovering from 33/4 before successfully chasing down a target of 131. articles.title: Marcus Trescothick says England opener may not have to be specialist
articles.summary: England’s Test opener does not necessarily have to be a specialist at the top of the order, according to Marcus Trescothick.
articles.body:
England's Test opener does not necessarily have to be a specialist at the top of the order, according to Marcus Trescothick.

England have a decision to make over how to accommodate Jacob Bethell when he returns from a knee injury for the tour of South Africa in December.

Emilio Gay, in his first summer as a Test cricketer, has opened alongside Ben Duckett. Gay has made three half-centuries, though he ends the season with an average below 25.

Duckett, one of England's senior players, made the team's only century of the summer, against New Zealand at Trent Bridge in June. However, the 31-year did not reach 20 in the three-match series against Pakistan and averages less than 24 since the beginning of the Ashes.

Jordan Cox has impressed as Bethell's replacement at number three. After finally making his debut this summer, Cox has averaged more than 42 and opened in first-class cricket early in his career.

Bethell has been touted as a potential opener and has moved up to open in England's one-day team.

The other new member of England's top six for the Pakistan series, Dan Lawrence, may be exempt from conversations over who is squeezed out because of the off-spin he offers, though Bethell's return would also bring some left-arm spin.

Trescothick has been England's interim coach for the Pakistan series and will now hand the reins to New Zealander Stephen Fleming, who is due to travel to the UK in the coming days to begin planning for the trip to South Africa.

"You generally want your best top seven, however that looks," said Trescothick. "Who that's going to be, I don't know. That's for someone else to work out."

Trescothick is one of England's most successful Test openers and was part of the team that famously won the 2005 Ashes. The former Somerset man believes the game is different to when he ended his 76-Test career in 2006.

"I reckon times have changed a little bit," said the 50-year-old. "I think you look at your best batting line-up, however that fits up.

"If that's with a specialist opener, great. If not, I think you can plan around it in this day and age. Players adapt pretty quickly because they're chopping and changing formats."

England chasing the rainbow with more questions than answers

England in better place than start of summer - Root

Fleming was appointed England's new Test coach in July, yet he missed the 3-0 series win against Pakistan.

The former New Zealand captain will now arrive for meetings with the England hierarchy.

He is expected to watch some of England's white-ball series against Sri Lanka, with the ODI and T20 teams still led by Fleming's fellow Kiwi and good friend Brendon McCullum. Fleming could also visit some of the counties.

When McCullum was in charge of both the Test and white-ball teams, he kept the same backroom team across formats, including Trescothick as an assistant.

However, it now looks likely that the staff will be reorganised. Former Australia batter Mike Hussey said he was approached by Fleming, though it has been reported down under that Hussey has declined.

Trescothick said he has not got clarity on his future role. He confirmed he has a preference but declined to reveal it.

"It's probably best I don't mention it at the moment because it may not be the case of what happens," he said. "I love doing both formats. It's brilliant and I've been privileged to be in the position of assistant coach."

Trescothick will be joined on England's staff by former team-mate Kevin Pietersen, who has been appointed as a consultant for the white-ball team.

Pietersen, one of the most flamboyant and innovative batters to play for England, returns to the national team 12 years after he was effectively sacked following the 5-0 Ashes defeat in 2013-14.

The 46-year-old's first day back in the England set-up is on Sunday, joining preparations for the first T20 against Sri Lanka in Southampton on Tuesday.

"We've spoken already, to plan a little bit," said Trescothick. "I gave him a couple of things that I wanted him to look at, to get his advice on.

"He is buzzing. Putting back on the shirt or the tracksuit, he is buzzing for that opportunity.

"Having his presence around and the knowledge he has about batting – he sees batting in a different light to many different people. If we can tap into that, it's only going to benefit the team."

articles.title: After Kagiso Rabada, South Africa lose another pacer as Ottneil Baartman ruled out of Australia ODIs
articles.summary: Cricket News: South Africa have suffered a fresh injury setback ahead of their three-match ODI series against Australia, with seamer Ottneil Baartman ruled out afte.
articles.body: South Africa have suffered a fresh injury setback ahead of their three-match ODI series against Australia, with seamer Ottneil Baartman ruled out after sustaining a left hamstring injury.Cricket South Africa confirmed the development on Sunday, with Duan Jansen named as Baartman’s replacement in the squad. Jansen will join the South African camp in Durban on September 19 ahead of the series opener.Baartman ruled out with hamstring injuryBaartman was not part of South Africa’s ongoing ODI series against Namibia, which is their first 50-over assignment since the tour of India late last year. The seamer was part of that India tour but has not featured for South Africa since the T20I series against New Zealand in March.Baartman subsequently played in the Major League Cricket in June and July before returning to competitive cricket for the Dolphins in their opening CSA 4-Day Series Division 1 fixture against the Titans this week.However, he bowled only five overs in the Titans' sole innings and did not return to bat in the Dolphins' second innings. CSA subsequently confirmed that the 32-year-old had suffered a hamstring injury.Duan Jansen gets another opportunityJansen, meanwhile, has been rewarded for his impressive performances during South Africa's ongoing limited-overs campaign. The left-arm seamer made his ODI debut against Namibia and immediately made an impact, finishing with figures of 4/31 in the second match of the three-game series.With South Africa already 2-0 ahead in the series, Jansen was one of three changes made for the final ODI. His latest call-up gives him an opportunity to stake a claim for a regular place in South Africa's ODI setup ahead of a challenging series against Australia.South Africa already without Kagiso RabadaBaartman's injury adds to South Africa's concerns in the pace department, with Kagiso Rabada also unavailable as he continues his recovery from a hamstring injury. South Africa have recalled Gerald Coetzee, who has not played an ODI since the 2023 World Cup.Anrich Nortje was not considered for selection, while the other pace options in the squad include Marco Jansen, Lungi Ngidi, Kwena Maphaka and Corbin Bosch. The combination will now face a major test against an Australian batting line-up in home conditions.Australia ODI series begins on September 24The three-match ODI series between South Africa and Australia will begin on September 24 in Durban. The second ODI will be played in Johannesburg on September 27, before the series concludes in Potchefstroom on September 30.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: South Africa cruise to nine-wicket win over Namibia, complete dominant 3-0 ODI series sweep
articles.summary: Cricket News: South Africa wrapped up their ODI series against Namibia in emphatic fashion on Sunday, cruising to a nine-wicket win in the third match to complete a.
articles.body: South Africa wrapped up their ODI series against Namibia in emphatic fashion on Sunday, cruising to a nine-wicket win in the third match to complete a 3-0 clean sweep. Bjorn Fortuin set up the victory with a four-wicket haul before Jordan Hermann and Connor Esterhuizen powered through the chase with an explosive 150-run opening stand.Maphaka, Bosch strike early for South AfricaAfter winning the toss and choosing to bat, Namibia struggled to build momentum against South Africa's disciplined bowling attack. Kwena Maphaka and Corbin Bosch made early inroads, reducing the hosts to 19/2.Alexander Busing-Volschenk and Louren Steenkamp then attempted to rebuild the innings, putting together a 53-run partnership that briefly steadied Namibia. But their resistance was short-lived.Fortuin triggers Namibia collapseFortuin broke the partnership in the 21st over by dismissing Steenkamp for 23. Namibia suffered another setback in the same over when Volschenk was run out for 31. Fortuin then struck again in his following over, removing Namibia captain Gerhard Erasmus for just three runs. The spinner continued to run through the middle order, dismissing Jan Nicol Loftie-Eaton (4) and Waldo Smith (2) to finish with impressive figures of 4/33 from 10 overs.Zane Green offered some resistance with a 33-ball effort from 42 deliveries, but Namibia were eventually bowled out for 156 in 36.2 overs. Maphaka finished with 2/18, while Bosch claimed 1/24.Hermann, Esterhuizen make light work of chaseSouth Africa's response was emphatic. Openers Jordan Hermann and Connor Esterhuizen immediately put Namibia under pressure, attacking from the beginning and building a huge 150-run opening partnership in just 21 overs.Hermann was particularly aggressive, smashing 13 boundaries during his 59-ball 77. He was eventually dismissed by Waldo Smith with South Africa needing only seven more runs for victory. Esterhuizen remained unbeaten on 68 off 68 balls, striking four fours and three sixes to anchor the chase.Brevis seals nine-wicket victory in styleWith just seven runs required, Dewald Brevis needed only two deliveries to finish the contest. The youngster launched his second ball for a six as South Africa reached 157/1 in 21.3 overs, winning by nine wickets with 29.3 overs still remaining.The victory completed a comprehensive 3-0 ODI series win for South Africa. They had begun the series with a 99-run DLS victory in the opening ODI before producing an even bigger margin of victory in the second match, winning by 157 runs.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Why Vande Mataram was sung before National Anthem in India vs Afghanistan T20I in Delhi - EXPLAINED
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: The National Song, Vande Mataram, was sung for the first time at an international cricket match before India's opening T20I against Afghani.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The National Song, Vande Mataram, was sung for the first time at an international cricket match before India's opening T20I against Afghanistan at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in New Delhi on Sunday. The three-match T20I series began with an unusual moment as the two teams lined up on the field before the start of the match.The National Anthem was played after Vande Mataram ended.Vande Mataram and National Anthem sung togetherThe development came after the Ministry of Home Affairs issued a notification earlier this year regarding Vande Mataram, India’s National Song.In a directive dated January 28, the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) laid down protocols for singing the National Song. It said six stanzas of Vande Mataram should be sung at official functions.It takes around 3 minutes and 10 seconds to sing all six stanzas of the song.The ministry listed events and situations where the National Song had to be sung along with the National Anthem. Sporting events were not included in the list.Vande Mataram and Jana Gana Mana were sung together in full for the first time on August 15, 2026, after Prime Minister Narendra Modi delivered his Independence Day speech.India opt to field against AfghanistanThe unusual start was followed by the toss, with India winning it and opting to field first.Jasprit Bumrah returned to the India playing XI for his first T20I appearance since IPL 2026. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi missed out, with Sanju Samson selected in his place despite the youngster's impressive performances in the Zimbabwe T20I series.India are the designated away side for the series, while Afghanistan are the official home team even though the matches are being played in Delhi.Why is Vaibhav Sooryavanshi not playing?India captain Shreyas Iyer said the team decided to bowl first after considering the conditions in Delhi. He also spoke about the positives from the Zimbabwe series and Bumrah's return.“We are going to bowl first. Whenever you come to Delhi, you know what the pitch has got to offer; it usually is a bowl-first wicket. We had a lot of positives in Zimbabwe; we will try and continue on that. We know Bumrah is a match-winner. Vaibhav is not playing, Washington is not playing, and two more,” Iyer said at the toss presentations.India vs Afghanistan 1st T20I playing XIs:India: Sanju Samson (w), Abhishek Sharma, Ishan Kishan, Shreyas Iyer (c), Tilak Varma, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Shivam Dube, Axar Patel, Arshdeep Singh, Jasprit Bumrah, Varun Chakaravarthy.Afghanistan: Ibrahim Zadran (c), Rahmanullah Gurbaz (w), Sediqullah Atal, Darwish Rasooli, Azmatullah Omarzai, Gulbadin Naib, Mohammad Nabi, Rashid Khan, Mujeeb Ur Rahman, Noor Ahmad, Fazalhaq Farooqi.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Cricket News: Shafali Verma produced another explosive batting display in the Women’s T20 Asia Cup final, smashing the fastest fifty in the history of the tournamen.
articles.body: Shafali Verma produced another explosive batting display in the Women’s T20 Asia Cup final, smashing the fastest fifty in the history of the tournament before departing for a blistering 68 off 39 balls against Sri Lanka. The India opener reached her half-century in just 24 balls, surpassing the previous record of 25 balls held by her opening partner Smriti Mandhana, who achieved the feat against Sri Lanka in Sylhet in 2022.Shafali's record-breaking fifty was built around a relentless boundary assault as she took the attack to the Sri Lankan bowlers during India's power-packed start.Shafali rewrites Asia Cup recordShafali's 24-ball fifty now stands alone as the fastest half-century in Women's T20 Asia Cup history.Fastest 50s in Women’s T20 Asia Cup (by balls faced)24 - Shafali Verma (IND-W) vs SL-W, Dubai, 202625 - Smriti Mandhana (IND-W) vs SL-W, Sylhet, 202226 - Richa Ghosh (IND-W) vs UAE-W, Dambulla, 202426 - Shafali Verma (IND-W) vs NEP-W, Dambulla, 202426 - Shafali Verma (IND-W) vs THA-W, Dubai, 2026Shafali equals Athapaththu's recordShafali's 68 also gave her a third 50-plus score in the ongoing tournament, putting her level with Sri Lanka captain Chamari Athapaththu for the most 50-plus scores in a single edition of the Women's T20 Asia Cup. Athapaththu had recorded three such scores during Sri Lanka's title-winning campaign in 2024. Shafali has now matched that mark in the 2026 edition, with the final still underway.Shafali, Smriti smash record partnershipThe India openers also established a new record partnership in the Women's T20 Asia Cup. Shafali and Smriti Mandhana put together 129 runs, the highest partnership for any wicket in the history of the tournament.
